extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and readers of philosophy and psychology (readers of William James)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and methodological guidance for evaluating claims about reality, causation, and the reality of activities/agents (e.g., selves, ideas, nerve-cells) in empirical and metaphysical inquiry. Focuses on pragmatic tests, empirical locating of causation, and limits of applying abstract logical axioms to concrete change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pragmatic test of hypotheses about agency
rubrics_metrics.description: What practical difference ought it to make if, instead of saying naively that 'I' am active now in delivering this address, I say that a wider thinker is active, or that certain ideas are active, or that certain nerve-cells are active, in producing the result?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate alternative accounts of agency by their pragmatic meaning — i.e., by the practical consequences they imply. Ask how each hypothesis affects expectations about continuity of purpose, responsibility, foreseeability of results, and whether the supposed agents would prolong or vitiate current aims (examples: wider thinker tends to corroborate and prolong purposes; ideas or nerve-cells as short-span agents give no guarantee of prolonged purposive outcome).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion of real activity (effectual causation as experienced)
rubrics_metrics.description: Real effectual causation as an ultimate nature is 'just what we feel it to be' — the conjunction revealed in our own activity-series; sustaining, persevering, striving, paying with effort, and achieving intention are action and effectuation in the only shape in which a pure experience-philosophy can discuss causality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the immediate lived impression of causation as a legitimate datum: if a process is experienced as efficacious, that experience supplies the notion of causation to be used unless empirical investigation shows otherwise. Do not dismiss felt efficacy outright as mere illusion without explaining what would replace it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical locating of effectuation and causal agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete philosophical questions should be: where is effectuation in this world located, which things are the true causal agents there, and what do the more remote effects consist of?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve metaphysical disputes by empirical investigation of the details of fact — examine which tendencies actually steer outcomes in particular cases rather than relying on abstract doctrine. Philosophical knowledge of general tendencies cannot substitute for case-level empirical inquiry when predicting which tendencies will prevail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical usefulness test for metaphysical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: If we could know what causation really and transcendentally is in itself, the only use of the knowledge would be to help us to recognize an actual cause when we had one, and so to track the future course of operations more intelligently out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge metaphysical claims by whether they improve our ability to identify causes and predict or track operations. Metaphysical inquiry lacking such pragmatic utility is not inherently more 'sublime' than other abstract inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning against reifying principles that duplicate phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: To explain a given fact by invoking a principle whose content simply rehearses the fact (a 'previous little spiritual copy of the fact') is animism in another shape and offers no genuine explanatory advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid positing ontological principles that merely restate observed phenomena; require that any proposed transphenomenal principle add independent explanatory or predictive power, not merely echo the phenomenon it purports to explain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axiom of skipped intermediaries and limits of serial transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'axiom of skipped intermediaries and transferred relations' (e.g., 'what is of a kind is of that kind's kind'; 'the cause of a cause is the cause of its effects') holds infallibly for certain abstract/pure series but cannot be applied offhand to concrete objects with numerous properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying serial/logical principles to concrete phenomena, inspect for changing 'aspects' that break straight-line substitution. Examples: chain-of-causation arguments can swerve into different respects; Commodore Perry as cause of Russian Douma is misleading across remote historical distances. Use caution and avoid unqualified transfer of relations across complex, multi-aspect systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reality-as-changing: expect failure of literal sameness and transferred causation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the practical world, terms and relations change so that 'sames of the same are certainly not sames of one another' over extended series; remoter effects are seldom aimed at by causal intentions and 'no one kind of causal activity continues indefinitely.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume long-range identity or unbroken causal transmission; accept that identities and relations 'give out' as otherness infiltrates and warps development. The result is that literal, indefinitely prolonged serial relations are generally inapplicable to living/historical phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for novelty via continuity (Peirce/Bergson synthesis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty does not appear ex nihilo in jumps; combined doctrines of tychism (chance/novelty) and synechism (continuity) yield 'agapasticism' or 'évolution créatrice' — novelty 'leaks in insensibly' and differentiation grows via infinitesimal tendencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When explaining creative novelty, prefer models that reconcile continuity with genuine emergence: expect gradual, interfused changes rather than abrupt breaking of continuity. Accordingly, historical/scientific projections must be approximate or statistical rather than literally exact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research agenda: relation of long-span to short-span activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Key empirical questions include whether, when ideas or wider activities appear confluent with smaller ones, the smaller activities coexist with, are steered by, or are supplanted by the wider ones; and whether mental activity-processes steer neural processes or short-circuit them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these as empirical problems requiring investigation in particular circumstances (examples: brain-cell chains affecting speech, thrombus altering statesman's action). Do not presume answers from metaphysical preference — document instances and mechanisms where long-span tendencies successfully guide or fail to guide short-span processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological caution: avoid forcing abstract straight-lines onto the 'zigzag' of reality
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempting to keep serial lines 'straight' through the changing, multi-aspect world does violence to its spontaneous development; trying to prolong a single directional line of historical development into the future yields unreal 'scientific' history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor flexible, context-sensitive, and often statistical descriptions of development over rigid literal extrapolation. Recognize that tracing a single invariant line of sameness or causation through historical/concrete series is typically impractical and misleading.
